question: Name the satellite launched by NASA to precisely track Earth's shrinking polar ice cover.
solution:
The correct answer is __**ICESat-2**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• NASA launched the ICESat-2 (Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite-2) to precisely track Earth’s polar ice cover and monitor changes in ice sheet elevation, sea ice thickness, and other land and sea ice characteristics.
 
• Launched in 2018, ICESat-2 uses advanced laser technology to measure the height of polar ice with unprecedented accuracy, helping scientists understand how melting ice impacts sea-level rise and climate patterns.
 
• It builds on data from its predecessor, ICESat, which operated from 2003 to 2010,
 
 
• and aims to provide detailed information on how climate change is affecting the planet's ice-covered regions.
 
 
 
• ICESat-2 uses an instrument called the **Advanced Topographic Laser Altimeter System (ATLAS)**,
 
 
• which emits 10,000 laser pulses per second toward the Earth’s surface.
 
 
 
• The laser measures the time it takes for each pulse to bounce back from the ground or ice surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CYGNSS (Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System)**:

 
 
• Launched by NASA in 2016, CYGNSS is a constellation of eight microsatellites designed to study tropical cyclones,
 
 
• specifically to understand their formation and intensity.
 
 
 
• CYGNSS uses signals from GPS satellites that bounce off the ocean surface to measure wind speed near the ocean's surface.
 
• This data provides insights into hurricane dynamics and helps improve storm forecasting.
 
 
 
• **SLINEX-2018**:
 
 
• SLINEX refers to a series of joint naval exercises between **India and Sri Lanka**.
 
• "SLINEX" stands for Sri Lanka–India Naval Exercise.
 
• The SLINEX exercises include training for maritime security, anti-submarine warfare, and search and rescue operations.
 
 
 
• **HYSIS (Hyperspectral Imaging Satellite)**:
 
 
• Launched by ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) in 2018, HYSIS was India’s first hyperspectral imaging satellite.
 
• HYSIS can capture images in multiple spectral bands across the visible and near-infrared regions.
 
• This allows it to identify and analyze materials based on their unique spectral signatures, making it useful for applications in agriculture, forestry, and environmental monitoring.
